# #3793: Patch: the AI's count of next turn's attacks leaves out a unit its Brittle destroys before it can swing
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Some units crumble on a timer. At the start of their owner's turn the count drops, and at zero the unit is destroyed, before it can attack. When the computer opponent works out how hard your board could hit it next turn, it still counts a unit that will crumble first.

For example, a grown Corpse Eater has Rush and Brittle 1, so it is destroyed at the start of its owner's next turn and can never hit a hero. At 8 attack it still makes the AI believe it faces lethal. The AI then pulls its own units back into Defense and passes up attacks it should make. Once this is built, the AI counts only the units that will still be standing when their turn's attacks come. The AI's own crumbling units stop counting as pressure too.

## Why

- `can_swing` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:125-132`) checks Can't attack, E35 and Frozen-through-next-turn, but not Brittle. `face_threat_with` (`evaluate.rs:927-941`) and `could_attack_next_turn` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:996-1001`) take it as "may swing next turn".
- `wall_switches` (`candidates.rs:962`) and `stands_down` (`candidates.rs:938`) build their Defense switches from that count. `lethal_threat` is 150 (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:660`).
- Nothing in `crates/ai/src` reads when a Brittle tick is due. `brittle_share` (`evaluate.rs:118`) only discounts the unit's worth.
- The rule: §6.1's Brittle row (`spec/06-keywords.md:56`). The tick runs at the start of the controller's turn, after the mana refresh, from turn t + 2 (`BRITTLE_FIRST_TICK_TURNS`, `crates/engine/src/config.rs:576`), and at 0 the card is destroyed. Indestructible ignores it (R46).
- Cards: Core #89 Corpse Eater (Rush, Brittle 1, grows in hand; `spec/08-catalog.md:140`), S #101 Overdrive Module (Brittle 2, then 1; `:686`), and any unit given Brittle by an effect.
- The search replays the opponent's reply through the real `reduce`, which sees the crumble. But the beam's static ranking and the wall and stand-down candidates are built from this count first, so phantom-lethal lines take beam slots (width 4) that real lines needed.

## Proposal

- Add a helper: the unit is destroyed by its own Brittle tick before its controller's next attacks. That means its active count is 1, its tick is due by that turn's start, and the destroy would take it (not Indestructible, R46). It reads the engine's Brittle state (`active_brittle_count` and the count's start). If the engine lacks a read for "tick due by turn N", that read goes into `crates/engine/src/query.rs` with its test.
- `face_threat_with` and `could_attack_next_turn` skip such a unit. `unit_worth` is left alone, since its Brittle share already discounts the unit.
- Gate it behind an `EvalWeights` flag, on in `AI_EVAL` and off in `GREEDY_EVAL`, as `gauntlet_bars_face_attacks` was (`config.rs:362,540,780`), so the greedy baseline stays frozen.
- A ruling in this issue's block on the §9.9 reading, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<N>.md`.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/`, possibly `crates/engine/src/query.rs`. SPEC §6.1 (Brittle), §9.9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An enemy Brittle-1 unit whose tick falls before its next turn's attacks adds 0 to `face_threat`, and `wall_switches` and `stands_down` offer no switch on its account.
- [ ] The same unit with its first tick not yet due still counts, and so does an Indestructible one.
- [ ] The AI's own such unit adds no lethal pressure.
- [ ] `GREEDY_EVAL`'s decisions are unchanged (flag off).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo jackioh gate` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green.

## Size and risks

Small to medium: one helper, two call sites, one flag, tests. `difficulty:hard` (the AI). Risk: getting the tick's turn wrong around extra turns. The helper reads the engine's own count and start rather than re-deriving them, and a test covers an extra turn if the engine counts one as a turn start.

## Goal

If a unit's own Brittle tick will destroy it at the start of its controller's next turn, before it can attack, the AI stops counting its attacks. It adds 0 to `face_threat` and to the evaluation's threat and pressure terms, and `could_attack_next_turn` rejects it, so `wall_switches` and `stands_down` offer no switch because of it. This holds for enemy units and for the AI's own.

These units still count:
- a unit whose first tick is not due yet;
- a unit the tick only lowers (count 2 or more);
- an Indestructible unit (R46);
- a unit of the player on turn when the evaluation reads that player as swinging first (`NextSwing`). That player attacks this turn, before any tick.

The new `EvalWeights` flag `brittle_crumbles_before_swing` turns this on. It is true in `AI_EVAL` and false in `GREEDY_EVAL`. `unit_worth` and `can_swing` do not change. Ruling R3793000 records the reading.

   /// R845, §2.2: every turn start, an extra turn's too, numbers the next turn (`state.turn`). The player not
   /// on turn starts at the next number; the player on turn at the one after the other player's turn.
   const NEXT_START_TURNS: i32 = 1;
   const OWN_NEXT_START_TURNS: i32 = 2;

   /// R3793000: whether the unit's own Brittle tick destroys it before its controller's next attacks:
   /// its count in force is at most one tick (`BRITTLE_TICK`; a count at 0 crumbles at its tick too), that
   /// tick is due (`brittle_due_by`) at the controller's next start, and it is not Indestructible (R46). With

   /// (R846). One owed to the other player only puts a start later, and a tick due earlier is due later too,
   /// so it is left out: it can only leave a doomed unit counted, as before.
   pub(crate) fn crumbles_before_swing(
       state: &GameState,
       unit: &CardInstance,
       view: &UnitView,
       on_turn_swings: bool,
   ) -> bool {
       if !active_brittle_count(unit).is_some_and(|count| count <= BRITTLE_TICK)
           || has_keyword(&view.keywords, KeywordKind::Indestructible)
       {
           return false;
       }
       let on_turn = state.active == unit.controller;
       if on_turn && on_turn_swings {
           return false;
       }
       let owes_extra = state.players[unit.controller].extra_turns.unwrap_or(0) > 0;
       let wait = if on_turn && !owes_extra { OWN_NEXT_START_TURNS } else { NEXT_START_TURNS };
       brittle_due_by(unit, state.turn + wait)
   }

## Goal

If a unit's own Brittle tick will destroy it at the start of its controller's next turn, before it can attack, the AI stops counting its attacks. It adds 0 to `face_threat` and to the evaluation's threat and pressure terms, and `could_attack_next_turn` rejects it, so `wall_switches` and `stands_down` offer no switch because of it. This holds for enemy units and for the AI's own.

These units still count:
- a unit whose first tick is not due yet;
- a unit the tick only lowers (count 2 or more);
- an Indestructible unit (R46);
- a unit of the player on turn when the evaluation reads that player as swinging first (`NextSwing`). That player attacks this turn, before any tick.

The new `EvalWeights` flag `brittle_crumbles_before_swing` turns this on. It is true in `AI_EVAL` and false in `GREEDY_EVAL`. `unit_worth` and `can_swing` do not change. Ruling R3793000 records the reading.
